summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was admitted with persistent left lower quadrant abdominal pain two months postpartum, following a spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by preeclampsia and chorioamnionitis. She had recently restarted oral contraceptives and reported pain consistent with her known biopsy-proven endometriosis. Initial evaluation revealed tachycardia and mild hypovolemia, with labs showing mild metabolic acidosis and hypokalemia. Imaging, including pelvic ultrasound and CT abdomen/pelvis, showed no acute surgical or infectious etiology. The pain was managed with NSAIDs, acetaminophen, tramadol, lidocaine patch, and PRN morphine, with gradual improvement. Tachycardia resolved with IV fluids and pain control. A single episode of minor rectal bleeding was noted but deemed self-limited. The patient was discharged home after three days with a plan to continue pain management and follow up with gynecology, with no new diagnoses established beyond a possible endometriosis flare.
